name: Can you get pool resurfacing done without making a mess in the yard?

mainEntity.name: How do contractors protect landscaping, pavers, and outdoor living areas during a resurfacing project?
mainEntity.text: How do contractors protect landscaping, pavers, and outdoor living areas during a resurfacing project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pool resurfacing can create dust, debris, slurry, and heavy equipment traffic, so site protection matters, especially on landscaped or high-end properties. Contractors should plan access routes, protect pavers and plantings, and manage disposal so the project does not damage the surrounding yard. In dense neighborhoods and upscale homes, this is more than a convenience issue because repairs to hardscape or landscaping can quickly add cost. Homeowners should ask exactly how the crew will protect the property, where materials will be staged, and how cleanup will be handled each day. A contractor who talks clearly about protection and access is usually more prepared than one who focuses only on the finish material and price.
acceptedAnswer.description: A well-managed resurfacing job should include protection for landscaping, hardscape, gates, and nearby outdoor features. Crews should control dust, debris, slurry, and equipment access so the yard is not damaged. The cleaner the site setup, the less likely the project is to create costly cleanup or repairs.
